fair_value_policy: Fair Value V2.1 is the sole valuation baseline. Semantic scores in this file must not directly overwrite official numeric macro series or Fair Value.
summary: Material change is dominated by the Federal Reserve's September 16 rate hike and a further Russia-Ukraine refined-product supply shock. The FOMC unanimously raised the target range 25 bp to 3.75%-4.00% and signaled that further tightening is likely; September projections point to 4.00%-4.25% at end-2026 and end-2027. Separately, Reuters confirmed Rosneft's Syzran and Saratov refineries stopped processing after Ukrainian drone attacks, with Syzran repairs potentially taking at least a month. Saudi alternative routing via Oman remains a partial mitigation to Middle East crude-supply risk, but refined-product and inflation risks remain elevated.

macro_summary.taiwan_equity_implication: The Fed hike and guidance for further tightening raise discount-rate, dollar and global-liquidity pressure on long-duration Taiwan technology equities. Persistent diesel and jet-fuel supply stress remains negative for airlines and energy-intensive manufacturers, while shipping has mixed rerouting/freight-rate benefits versus bunker-cost inflation.
macro_summary.notes: Official numeric series remain authoritative. Reuters market observations and semantic scores are research evidence only.

key_drivers.name: Federal Reserve begins new tightening cycle
key_drivers.observed: The FOMC voted 12-0 to raise the federal funds target range 25 bp to 3.75%-4.00%. Reuters reported 16 of 18 policymakers expect at least one more hike by year-end and the projected policy-rate range is 4.00%-4.25% at end-2026 and end-2027.
key_drivers.interpretation: This materially raises global discount-rate and dollar pressure and makes a one-and-done hike less likely.

key_drivers.name: Russian refinery outages deepen
key_drivers.observed: Reuters reported Syzran and Saratov refineries stopped processing after Ukrainian drone attacks; Syzran's main CDU representing about 71% of capacity was damaged and repairs could take at least a month.
key_drivers.interpretation: This raises persistence of diesel/jet-fuel scarcity and freight/energy-inflation pressure.

key_drivers.name: Saudi alternative export routing via Oman
key_drivers.observed: Saudi Arabia is offering additional crude via ship-to-ship loading off Sohar outside Hormuz.
key_drivers.interpretation: Partial mitigation for crude availability, but not a resolution of Hormuz, Yanbu, East-West Pipeline or Red Sea risks.

key_risks: Further Fed hikes lift front-end yields, DXY and equity discount rates.
Energy inflation prevents monetary-policy relief and broadens beyond one-off supply effects.
Russian refinery outages and export restrictions sustain diesel/jet-fuel scarcity.
Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb security risks remain unresolved.
Taiwan central-bank decision is due September 17 and was not pre-assumed.
VIX, copper, USD/TWD and exact post-FOMC Treasury closes remain stale in this semantic snapshot.

policy_tone.fed: Hawkish tightening: target range raised to 3.75%-4.00%; further hikes indicated by September projections.
policy_tone.taiwan_central_bank: Decision due September 17; current policy rate remains 2.0% until an official decision changes it.
policy_tone.global: Energy shock remains inflationary and growth-negative while major central banks face renewed tightening pressure.

events.observed_evidence: Rosneft's Syzran and Saratov refineries stopped processing after Ukrainian drone attacks. Syzran's main CDU, about 71% of capacity, was damaged and repairs could take at least a month; Saratov has been halted since September 11.
events.semantic_interpretation: Confirmed multi-week refinery impairment reinforces the Russian refined-product shock and adds diesel, jet-fuel, freight and inflation pressure to the existing Middle East energy shock.
